sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: South Korea's Education Minister Resigns Over Cheating Scandal
cards.content: South Korea's Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin has resigned due to an exam cheating scandal. He took responsibility for the sudden measures taken to stop AI-assisted cheating during the annual college entrance exam, known as Suneung. The measures included sending emergency alerts to every mobile phone in the country, causing widespread alarm. A week ago, the top scorer in the national tax accountancy exam admitted using a mini-camera, mobile phone, and AI tools. This led to concerns over academic dishonesty during the fiercely competitive exam. The education ministry found 111 candidates with unauthorized devices during this year's Suneung, taken by about 500,000 students. The exam plays a big role in career trajectories of millions of South Koreans.

cards.title: White Evangelicals Back Republicans, but Party's Electoral College Risks Grow
cards.content: White evangelical Christians stuck with Republicans in the recent election, but this loyalty could be a double-edged sword for the GOP as they chart a path to recovery in 2028. While Republicans succeeded in holding evangelicals with a cultural message against Democrats, this strategy failed to overcome frustrations about the economy, war, and perceived corruption among non-evangelical voters. Democrats achieved historic breakthroughs among these voters, winning in previously red states across the South and Midwest. Unless Republicans can reverse Democratic inroads with non-evangelical voters, the Electoral College map in 2028 could look radically different, with Republicans struggling in states like Iowa, Ohio, and Texas. The GOP's problem is that cultural issues, which energize evangelicals, actively repel other voters who have traditionally supported the party. Meanwhile, Democrats are on track to win the national popular vote in House elections by a 14-point margin, the largest margin since the Democrats' 1974 post-Watergate landslide. The results highlight the GOP's risk of relying too heavily on White evangelicals, as their share of the overall US population has been declining since the 1990s.

cards.title: Russian Ship Hit by Drone Attack in Libyan Port
cards.content: a Russian ship docked in Benghazi naval base in Libya was hit by a suspected drone attack, causing an explosion and a fire, but no casualties were reported. The ship was stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia. The Libyan government has confirmed the incident and is investigating, with authorities coordinating with Russian counterparts to determine the source of the attack. Videos and satellite imagery show the ship engulfed in flames and smoke. The incident is seen as a possible violation of maritime safety and an attack on Libya's sovereignty. It has raised concerns about the risks of involving ports and civilian facilities in activities related to external conflicts.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Scientists reveal narwhal tusk's unique spiral structure
cards.content: Scientists have made a groundbreaking discovery about the internal structure of narwhal tusks, revealing two intertwined spirals that twist in opposite directions. This unique structure helps the enormous tooth withstand mechanical stress and provides a new explanation for the anatomy behind one of nature's most recognizable features. The findings, published in Nature Communications, offer a new perspective on the narwhal's tusk, which has fascinated scientists for years. The study also investigates how the tusk grows and how it can preserve a record of the Arctic environment over decades. The research team used a specialized X-ray technique to examine the microscopic building blocks of the tusk, and their findings provide new insights into the remarkable properties of the narwhal's tooth.

cards.title: IEA warns data center power demand may double by 2030
cards.content: The International Energy Agency warned that the global electricity use by data centers could double by 2030, potentially straining power grids and delaying new projects. The agency forecasts that data centers will consume around 1,000 terawatt-hours of electricity a year by 2030, citing large project pipelines in several regions. If grid upgrades are not made, power networks could become less reliable, and new projects may face longer waits to connect. The agency also projects that peak electricity demand will rise 40% to 50% by 2035, and grid spending is expected to rise 75% over the next decade. The IEA emphasized the importance of reliable power grids as countries seek to reduce their reliance on imported oil and gas through electrification.

cards.title: Estonian Tech Billionaire Jaan Tallinn to Gain Billions in Anthropic IPO
cards.content: Jaan Tallinn, an Estonian tech billionaire and AI safety advocate, is set to be one of the biggest winners in Anthropic's upcoming IPO, with his initial investment potentially returning tens of billions. Tallinn co-founded Skype and led Anthropic's first funding round, five years ago, before the company's Claude chatbot became a market success. Anthropic's IPO, set to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT, is expected to be the largest in history, valuing the company at around $1.4 trillion. Tallinn's exact return will depend on the level of dilution in subsequent funding rounds and whether he sold any shares. Despite his concerns about AI's existential risk, Tallinn's investment in Anthropic has paid off, and he will benefit from the company's commercial success, which some worry may come at the expense of AI safety.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Frequent Short Walks Boost Blood Sugar Control, Study Shows
cards.content: Scientists have discovered that taking frequent short walks throughout the day can improve blood sugar control, particularly for people at risk of type 2 diabetes. In a study, participants were assigned to either walk for 45 minutes once a day or in 5-minute breaks throughout the day. The group that took frequent breaks saw a significant increase in time spent within a target blood sugar range, from 82% to 94%, whereas the group that walked in one continuous session experienced a decline. The study suggests that distributing physical activity throughout the day may be as important as the total amount of exercise, and that interrupting prolonged sitting with short walks may offer additional benefits for glucose regulation.

cards.title: CP research challenges previous findings, suggests complex condition
cards.content: New research on cerebral palsy (CP) challenges previous findings and proposes a different understanding of the condition. The study, published in the American Journal of Human Genetics, found that only 89 out of 515 previously linked genes showed a statistically significant association with CP. The researchers suggest that CP may not be a single disease, but rather a collection of symptoms arising from multiple underlying conditions. They propose a 'phenotypic paradigm' for understanding CP, considering it a clinical characteristic that can emerge from different genetic disorders and environmental influences. The study's findings do not disprove connections between CP and other genes, but rather highlight the need for further research and validation before these findings can be applied to patient care.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Ministers Urge COP31 to Advance Fossil Fuel Transition
cards.content: In a significant move, over 10 ministers have urged the presidencies of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to advance roadmaps for transitioning away from fossil fuels. This follows announcements from Denmark, Luxembourg, Spain, and Portugal of new national plans. Meanwhile, developing nations are demanding greater financial support for a fair transition. The UN climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, is seeing growing political support for turning last year's COP28 commitment into national action plans. However, negotiations at COP31 have exposed divisions over how to implement the commitment, including concerns over international roadmaps constraining national energy policies and financing for developing countries.

cards.title: Human metabolism's carbon dioxide emissions rise 74% in 30 years
cards.content: A new study by the University of Bath has found that the amount of carbon dioxide produced by human metabolism has increased by 74% over the past three decades, with the global total reaching an estimated 2.05 billion metric tons annually by 2015. The study, published in The Lancet Planetary Health, analyzed thousands of real-world measurements of CO2 production in people of all ages and found that the increase is mainly due to population growth, with more than 60% of the rise attributed to an increase in the number of people rather than a significant change in the amount produced by each individual. The researchers suggest that accounting for this activity could help scientists more accurately predict how effective carbon reduction strategies may be.

cards.title: Srinagar's Water Crisis Worsens due to Climate Change
cards.content: In Srinagar, a water crisis has been ongoing for years, causing daily struggles for residents like Mehak and Zamrood. The absence of a regular water supply has led to the installation of tanks and a hand pump at their homes. Climate change is affecting Doodh Ganga, a vital source of drinking water, causing erratic water supply, low flow, and dry taps. The river's water availability is decreasing due to rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and declining snowmelt. The Kashmir Valley's 24 watersheds, including Doodh Ganga, are experiencing similar impacts.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: BBC apologizes for lewd audio disruption on Strictly Come Dancing
cards.content: The BBC apologized for any offense caused after a live broadcast of Strictly Come Dancing was disrupted by lewd audio sounds from the audience in Blackpool's Tower Ballroom. Judge Motsi Mabuse paused during the episode and joked about the noises, while presenter Emma Willis later apologized to viewers for any disruptions. The incident was captured by a social media content creator who has been involved in similar pranks before. The BBC is investigating how this happened and an edit will be made to the episode available on BBC iPlayer. Lancashire police are also assessing whether any criminal offenses took place and have seized a mobile phone as part of their inquiry.

cards.title: Twin brothers direct drama film 'Small Pond' in hometown Evesham
cards.content: Twin brothers Benji and Thom Parry, former musicians, are writing and directing a feature film called Small Pond. The drama is set in their hometown of Evesham, where they grew up and developed a passion for filmmaking. The story follows two musicians who form an unlikely friendship, and it's a personal reflection of Benji's own experiences. As a child, Benji made films with his parents' camcorder and later spent years performing in bands, which ultimately led him to pursue filmmaking. The film explores the struggles of chasing creative ambitions in a small town, and the Parry brothers believe the experience will resonate with many who have grown up in similar places. The production is filming at local Evesham locations and collaborating with local businesses, embracing their roots and creating a film that is deeply connected to their hometown.

cards.title: Miley Cyrus Marries Maxx Morando in Palm Springs
cards.content: Miley Cyrus, 33, has married her partner of four years, Maxx Morando, 28, in a ceremony in Palm Springs, California. The couple, who met on a blind date, exchanged vows surrounded by white roses and a golden retriever, with Morando's proposal being kept secret until the last moment. Miley's family, including her mother and sister, attended the ceremony, while her father was present with his partner Liz Hurley. The singer wore a Saint Laurent designed dress, and the couple shared photos of their special day on Instagram, with friends and family congratulating them in the comments.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: US Restricts Chip Access Amid China Intelligence Allegations
cards.content: Chinese leader Xi Jinping hosted US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, showcasing the country's technological advancements. However, the meeting came amid controversy surrounding allegations that Chinese intelligence had targeted the head of Nvidia, a US tech company. The US subsequently announced new licensing requirements to restrict Chinese access to advanced US chips. This development has reignited fears that America's best technology could fall into adversarial hands. The situation has complicated negotiations between the two nations, with China threatening to take countermeasures to safeguard its national sovereignty, security, and development interests. The fragile truce between the US and China has been put to the test, with both sides struggling to balance their economic interests and national security concerns.

cards.title: AI-Enhanced Images Raise Concerns of Misleading Homebuyers
cards.content: Estate agents are increasingly using AI to enhance property images, making homes seem more appealing. However, this practice, dubbed 'housefishing', has raised concerns among experts and homebuyers that it can mislead and waste time. Olivia Nicole, 29, was shocked to find that a five-bedroom property she viewed had been significantly altered from its online listing, with smaller rooms, different decor, and structural features changed. The AI-enhanced images, used on Rightmove, Zoopla, and Winkworth, were not clearly labeled as such, leading Olivia to feel her time was wasted. Experts warn that estate agents must use AI responsibly, labeling enhanced images and avoiding structural changes that can mislead consumers. As the trend continues to grow, concerns are rising that AI-enhanced images may become more widespread, potentially leading to more instances of 'housefishing'.

cards.title: Nscale to Build UK's Largest AI Data Centre in Loughton, Despite Microsoft Pullout
cards.content: Nscale, a tech company, has reaffirmed its plans to build the UK's largest AI data centre in Loughton, Essex, despite Microsoft's decision to pull out of the project. Microsoft had agreed to fund a supercomputer at the site, but its involvement has been terminated. Nscale is exploring alternative power sources and maintaining a strong relationship with Microsoft for other projects globally. The data centre was expected to receive its power supply by the end of this year, but this has been delayed until the 2030s due to a London-wide grid issue. The project is expected to create 250 permanent jobs when it opens.
